parsed.why: Strong state shield law, broad gender-identity anti-discrimination, hate-crime coverage and trans-panic repeal raise it above the parent; national passport/entry, facility and custody exposures plus an old birth-sex custody case keep it below Reduced Risk.

Most-protective tier with public-accommodations law, gender-neutral restroom rule, care shield, hate-crime coverage and trans-panic repeal. National border, facility and custody rules still impose traveler-facing exposure.

Most-protective tier with broad housing/accommodation anti-discrimination, care shield, hate-crime coverage, trans-panic repeal and no bathroom ban. National document, entry and custody regime remains the limiting exposure.

State care ban for minors, abrupt adult surgery cancellation, documented lethal violence against trans women and no cited statewide nondiscrimination or hate-crime protection place it below the parent. National framework still applies.

No statewide gender-identity nondiscrimination or hate-crime coverage, original-sex ID rule, minor-care and prison-care bans, sports ban and active bathroom-bill conflict. Below parent, barely above Do Not Travel band.
